saints.name: St. Pachomius
saints.title: Abbot
saints.shortBlurb: The Egyptian soldier-turned-hermit who gathered the desert solitaries into community and wrote monasticism's first Rule…
biography: Born of pagan parents in the Egyptian Thebaid about 292, Pachomius was conscripted at twenty into the army and held with other recruits at Thebes, where Christians brought the wretched youths food and comfort. Astonished at such charity toward strangers, he prayed to the Christians' God and vowed to serve Him all his days.

Released and baptized about 314, he placed himself under the aged hermit Palemon, from whom he learned the solitary life. About 320 he settled at Tabennisi on the Nile and there gathered his disciples into an ordered community, writing for them a Rule of prayer, labor, and common life — the earliest written rule of monasticism.

The work grew swiftly: before his death Pachomius governed nine monasteries of men and two of women, numbering many thousands of monks. Carried off by an epidemic in 348, he left a pattern that Basil shaped for the East and that Jerome, by translating the Rule into Latin, carried to the West, where it prepared the way for Benedict.
saints.knownFor: Founding cenobitic (communal) monasticism and its first written Rule.

sources.text: The Roman Martyrology (1914 English ed.; public domain)
